## 1. The descendants bear witness  (`#the-descendants-bear-witness`)

Cited ayat: 7:172-174

> **7:172** وَإِذْ أَخَذَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ مِن ظُهُورِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَأَشْهَدَهُمْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ أَلَسْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ قَالُوا۟ بَلَىٰ شَهِدْنَآ أَن تَقُولُوا۟ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّا كُنَّا عَنْ هَٰذَا غَٰفِلِينَ
>
> **7:173** أَوْ تَقُولُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَآ أَشْرَكَ ءَابَآؤُنَا مِن قَبْلُ وَكُنَّا ذُرِّيَّةً مِّنۢ بَعْدِهِمْ أَفَتُهْلِكُنَا بِمَا فَعَلَ ٱلْمُبْطِلُونَ
>
> **7:174** وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُفَصِّلُ ٱلْـَٔايَٰتِ وَلَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْجِعُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (7:172): God took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants.

**c2** (7:172): He made them bear witness over themselves, asking whether He was not their Lord, and they said yes, they bore witness.

**c3** (7:172): This was so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection that they had been unaware of this.

**c4** (7:173): It was also so that they would not say that only their forefathers had associated others with God before, and that they themselves were descendants after them, asking whether He would destroy them for what the falsifiers had done.

**c5** (7:174): God says that in this way He makes the signs clear in detail, so that perhaps they will return.

### One-minute summary

God took from the children of Adam their descendants and made them bear witness over themselves, asking whether He was not their Lord, and they said yes [c1][c2]. The Quran gives the purpose: that they could not say on the Day of Resurrection that they had been unaware [c3].

### Complete story

God took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants [c1]. He made them bear witness over themselves, asking whether He was not their Lord, and they said yes, they bore witness [c2].

The Quran gives the purpose [c3]. It was so that they would not say on the Day of Resurrection that they had been unaware of this [c3]. It was also so that they would not say that only their forefathers had associated others with God, and that they were descendants after them, and ask whether God would destroy them for what the falsifiers had done [c4]. God says that in this way He makes the signs clear in detail, so that perhaps they will return [c5].

### Deep study

The passage moves from the taking and the witnessing [c1][c2] to the excuses it closes off [c3][c4] and ends with a closing remark on the explaining of the signs [c5]. The verses speak of descendants taken from the loins of the children of Adam [c1]; they do not say how this relates to a person's later birth.

### Kids mode

God asked the children of Adam whether He was not their Lord, and they said yes [c1][c2]. This was so that nobody could say on the Day of Resurrection that they had not known [c3].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passage presents knowing God as a witness every person carries, so that ignorance is not a final excuse [c3]. Another is that blaming one's forefathers is closed off as a plea [c4].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: when, where or how the taking and the witnessing happened; the verses give no time, place or manner.
- Not established: how the taking of descendants from loins relates to a person's later birth or life; interpreters understand the passage in more than one way, and a scholar should decide how the page words it.
- Not established: who is meant by the falsifiers in the last excuse beyond the word itself.
- The verses do not use the word covenant; the inventory title reflects the usual name of the passage, which a reviewer may wish to word with care.
